newsitem.title: USA: Sony names Amy Pascal president of Columbia Pictures.
newsitem.headline: Sony names Amy Pascal president of Columbia Pictures.

text.p: Sony Pictures Entertainment Sunday named former Turner Pictures executive Amy Pascal as president of its troubled Columbia Pictures division.
The troubled studio, which has recently undergone a substantial management shakeup, said Pascal will report to new Sony Pictures Entertainment President John Calley.
She will succeed Lisa Henson, who left the studio earlier this year to form her own production company.
The move comes less than a month after Calley assumed control of Sony Pictures Entertainment, the umbrella company for Columbia and TriStar Pictures.

Pascal worked for Columbia Pictures for seven years before joining Turner Pictures in 1994 as president of production, overseeing development and production of more than two dozen films including the upcoming "Michael," starring John Travolta.
At Columbia, she was involved with a number of successful films, including "Little Women", "A League of their Own," and "Groundhog Day."
Sony officials are hoping she can repeat her previous success at Columbia, which has suffered this year from a series of disappointing films.
"Amy has a remarkable track record for developing and producing movies that are critical successes as well as audience pleasers," Calley said in a statement.
"She is a terrific executive who brings to Columbia Pictures the right combination of superior taste in material, great talent relationships and an innovative approach to filmmaking."
Sony said Pascal will work with Columbia-TriStar Vice Chairman Lucy Fisher and Executive Vice President Gareth Wigan and Production President Barry Josephson.
Earlier this summer, Sony named former HBO executive Robert Cooper president of TriStar.
Sony purchased Columbia Pictures in 1989 for $3.4 billion. Since then it has struggled to find the right management team to provide a steady stream of box office hits.
